topic: Why Sanad offices — 100% Omani-staffed, government-mandated — are the most important B2B channel in Oman that nobody has built software for yet
format: Client trust story: the Sanad office that started giving every client a portal to track their own cases — what happened to client retention and referrals in the first three months
post:
Before she touches her laptop, her phone is already blowing up.

Twenty client companies. Forty work permits. Fifteen visa renewals. Eight MOL filings. All of it living inside WhatsApp threads and a shared Excel file that three people are editing at the same time — overwriting each other's updates, losing rows, missing deadlines nobody knew were coming.

Her words: "Every morning I open my phone and I already feel behind."

So she made one change. She gave every client a portal where they could see their own cases.

Three months later, the "where is my file?" calls stopped. The calls she started getting instead were referrals.

That's not a small thing. That's the entire business model shifting — from spending your day answering status questions to actually doing the work. Clients who can see their cases moving don't need to chase you. And clients who don't need to chase you tell other people about you.

This is the gap sitting inside most of the 924 licensed Sanad offices in Oman right now. Not effort — there's plenty of that. Not capability. Just the infrastructure to show clients that the work is actually happening.

Work permit tracking used to be a differentiator. It's not anymore. Clients expect visibility. The offices that give it to them keep growing. The ones still running everything through memory and WhatsApp stay stuck at whatever volume one person can hold in their head on a good day.

The gap is real. And most of the market hasn't moved yet.
